english_classification.chapter_note: This chapter is predominantly institutional/editorial material explaining the cosmic significance of Manichaean liturgical practices (assent and amen). The substrate core is limited to ¶2-4: a compact teaching that maps assent→summons and amen→obedience (answer), then describes how these cosmic entities functioned as portals for the First Man's redemption and as purifiers of the living soul. From ¶5 onward, the teaching applies these cosmic archetypes to congregational worship practice — describing liturgical sealing, the formation of ascending images from collective sound, healing power, and overcoming temptation. All of this later material has one side of its mapping reaching into institutional practice ('the congregation', 'great crowds of people', 'the elect', 'their alms'). The text is heavily damaged throughout with extensive lacunae, especially ¶4 and ¶10-16. Substrate vocabulary is entirely concentrated in the first half (8.71→0.00), confirming the core teaching ends early. Gardner notes this chapter was completed from Funk's working text beyond the published edition.
